# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Daily Update (Feb 27, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
The day saw the introduction of a new feature related to zk dispute games. Discussions continued on an active issue concerning the `op-node`'s handling of safe and local_safe heads in lite mode, particularly in the context of interop.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Dispute Game Enhancements
A new feature was proposed to add zk dispute game functionality, indicating ongoing development in the dispute resolution mechanisms. ([#368](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/368))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
A new pull request, [#368](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/368), titled "feat: add zk dispute game", was opened. This PR introduces a new feature related to zero-knowledge dispute games.

## CLOSED ISSUES
None

## NEW ISSUES
None

## ACTIVE ISSUES
### Clarifying Safe Head Tracking in `op-node` Lite Mode ([#19325](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19325))
Discussions continued regarding how an `op-node` in lite mode, which follows a source instead of performing its own derivation, should handle `local_safe_l2` and `safe_l2` heads. The core of the issue revolves around the current behavior where the `safe_l2` of the source is used as the `local_safe_l2` of the destination, which may not be accurate, especially with interop.

`geoknee` clarified the terminology, distinguishing between "unqualified safe" (`SyncStatus.safe_l2`, representing a fully verified safe head) and "qualified safe" (`SyncStatus.local_safe_l2`, representing a head not yet interop-verified). They emphasized that in a supernode, virtual CLs track both, and it's crucial for the CL to differentiate them. The proposal is to ensure that the `local_safe_l2` of the light CL matches the `local_safe_l2` of the source, and similarly for `safe_l2`.

`pcw109550` validated their understanding, noting that for a leader sequencer, there are two levels of "safe" for interop: unqualified (derived from L1) and qualified (derived from L1 and passed interop verification). They also highlighted that the `optimism_syncStatus` RPC exposes the qualified `safe` for leader sequencers and the unqualified `safe` for non-leader sequencers and verifiers. The invariant `Qualified safe <= Unqualified safe <= Unsafe` was also noted. `pcw109550` acknowledged that for pre-interop, `local_safe_l2` and `safe_l2` being the same made sense, but with interop, distinguishing them and fine-graining external information injection is necessary.
